title: SmokePing — Overview
description: Latency distribution (the smoke graph), success rate, per-endpoint-IP comparison and per-vantage-point comparison. Backed by ClickHouse; see the README for the PostgreSQL equivalents.

list.name: location
list.label: Agent location
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT agent_location FROM smokeping.measurements ORDER BY agent_location

list.name: probe
list.label: Probe
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT probe FROM smokeping.measurements ORDER BY probe

list.name: target
list.label: Target
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT target_name FROM smokeping.measurements WHERE agent_location IN (${location:sqlstring}) AND probe IN (${probe:sqlstring}) ORDER BY target_name

panels.title: Smoke graph — latency distribution
panels.description: The original SmokePing view. Every individual round-trip time is unnested from rtts_ms, so the bands are a true distribution rather than a summary of summaries: min–max in light shading, the interquartile range darker, and the median as a line. A widening band means jitter even when the median is flat.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeInterval(ts) AS time,
  min(rtt)            AS "min",
  quantile(0.25)(rtt) AS "p25",
  quantile(0.50)(rtt) AS "median",
  quantile(0.75)(rtt) AS "p75",
  max(rtt)            AS "max"
FROM smokeping.measurements
ARRAY JOIN rtts_ms AS rtt
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts)
  AND agent_location IN (${location:sqlstring})
  AND probe          IN (${probe:sqlstring})
  AND target_name    IN (${target:sqlstring})
GROUP BY time
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Success rate
panels.description: Share of cycles where the probe produced a usable measurement. Partial packet loss still counts as a success — that is the signal, not an error.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT 100 * countIf(success = 1) / count() AS success_rate
FROM smokeping.measurements
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts)
  AND agent_location IN (${location:sqlstring})
  AND probe          IN (${probe:sqlstring})
  AND target_name    IN (${target:sqlstring})

SELECT quantile(0.5)(latency_ms) AS median_ms
FROM smokeping.measurements
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts)
  AND success = 1
  AND agent_location IN (${location:sqlstring})
  AND probe          IN (${probe:sqlstring})
  AND target_name    IN (${target:sqlstring})

SELECT avg(loss_pct) AS loss_pct
FROM smokeping.measurements
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts)
  AND packets_sent > 0
  AND agent_location IN (${location:sqlstring})
  AND probe          IN (${probe:sqlstring})
  AND target_name    IN (${target:sqlstring})

SELECT
  $__timeInterval(ts) AS time,
  target_name,
  avg(loss_pct) AS loss_pct
FROM smokeping.measurements
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts)
  AND packets_sent > 0
  AND agent_location IN (${location:sqlstring})
  AND probe          IN (${probe:sqlstring})
  AND target_name    IN (${target:sqlstring})
GROUP BY time, target_name
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Failures by error type
panels.description: Every failed probe is stored, with a canonical error_type. Grouping by it separates 'DNS is broken' from 'the path is down' at a glance.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeInterval(ts) AS time,
  error_type,
  count() AS failures
FROM smokeping.measurements
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts)
  AND success = 0
  AND agent_location IN (${location:sqlstring})
  AND probe          IN (${probe:sqlstring})
  AND target_name    IN (${target:sqlstring})
GROUP BY time, error_type
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Per-endpoint IP comparison — which address is slow?
Latency by resolved IP
panels.description: One hostname behind anycast or a CDN is really N different services. resolved_ip records the address actually talked to, so a single degraded PoP or edge shows up as its own line instead of being averaged away.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeInterval(ts) AS time,
  concat(target_name, ' @ ', resolved_ip) AS endpoint,
  quantile(0.5)(latency_ms) AS median_ms
FROM smokeping.measurements
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts)
  AND success = 1
  AND resolved_ip != ''
  AND agent_location IN (${location:sqlstring})
  AND probe          IN (${probe:sqlstring})
  AND target_name    IN (${target:sqlstring})
GROUP BY time, endpoint
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Endpoint comparison
panels.description: Sorted by p95, worst first — the endpoints worth investigating are at the top.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  resolved_ip                                  AS "IP",
  any(target_name)                             AS "Target",
  any(ip_family)                               AS "Family",
  count()                                      AS "Samples",
  round(quantile(0.50)(latency_ms), 2)         AS "Median ms",
  round(quantile(0.95)(latency_ms), 2)         AS "p95 ms",
  round(avg(jitter_ms), 2)                     AS "Jitter ms",
  round(avg(loss_pct), 2)                      AS "Loss %",
  round(100 * countIf(success = 1) / count(), 2) AS "Success %"
FROM smokeping.measurements
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts)
  AND resolved_ip != ''
  AND agent_location IN (${location:sqlstring})
  AND probe          IN (${probe:sqlstring})
  AND target_name    IN (${target:sqlstring})
GROUP BY resolved_ip
ORDER BY "p95 ms" DESC
LIMIT 100

panels.title: Vantage point comparison — where does it look bad from?
Latency by agent location
panels.description: The same target measured from every vantage point. If one location diverges, the problem is the path from there — not the target.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeInterval(ts) AS time,
  agent_location,
  quantile(0.5)(latency_ms) AS median_ms
FROM smokeping.measurements
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts)
  AND success = 1
  AND agent_location IN (${location:sqlstring})
  AND probe          IN (${probe:sqlstring})
  AND target_name    IN (${target:sqlstring})
GROUP BY time, agent_location
ORDER BY time

SELECT
  agent_location                               AS "Location",
  uniq(agent_id)                               AS "Agents",
  uniq(target_name)                            AS "Targets",
  count()                                      AS "Samples",
  round(quantile(0.50)(latency_ms), 2)         AS "Median ms",
  round(quantile(0.95)(latency_ms), 2)         AS "p95 ms",
  round(avg(loss_pct), 2)                      AS "Loss %",
  round(100 * countIf(success = 1) / count(), 2) AS "Success %",
  max(ts)                                      AS "Last seen"
FROM smokeping.measurements
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts)
  AND probe       IN (${probe:sqlstring})
  AND target_name IN (${target:sqlstring})
GROUP BY agent_location
ORDER BY "p95 ms" DESC

panels.title: HTTP timing breakdown
panels.description: Stacked phases from curl: DNS, TCP connect, TLS handshake, server think time and body transfer. This is what turns 'the site got slow' into 'the TLS handshake got slow'.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeInterval(ts) AS time,
  round(avg(dns_ms), 2)                 AS "DNS",
  round(avg(tcp_connect_ms), 2)         AS "TCP connect",
  round(avg(tls_handshake_ms), 2)       AS "TLS handshake",
  round(avg(server_processing_ms), 2)   AS "Server processing",
  round(avg(content_transfer_ms), 2)    AS "Content transfer"
FROM smokeping.v_curl
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts)
  AND success = 1
  AND agent_location IN (${location:sqlstring})
  AND target_name    IN (${target:sqlstring})
GROUP BY time
ORDER BY time

panels.title: HTTP endpoints — status, final URL and edge IP
panels.description: url_effective exposes a target that has started redirecting somewhere unexpected; remote_ip identifies which CDN edge served it.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  target_name                          AS "Target",
  resolved_ip                          AS "Edge IP",
  any(http_code)                       AS "Status",
  any(http_version)                    AS "HTTP",
  any(url_effective)                   AS "Final URL",
  count()                              AS "Requests",
  round(quantile(0.50)(ttfb_ms), 1)    AS "TTFB p50",
  round(quantile(0.95)(total_ms), 1)   AS "Total p95",
  max(ts)                              AS "Last seen"
FROM smokeping.v_curl
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts)
  AND agent_location IN (${location:sqlstring})
  AND target_name    IN (${target:sqlstring})
GROUP BY target_name, resolved_ip
ORDER BY "Total p95" DESC
LIMIT 100

panels.title: DNS latency by responding server
panels.description: 8.8.8.8 is dozens of machines. This groups by the resolver that actually answered, which is the only way to see a single bad anycast PoP.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeInterval(ts) AS time,
  dns_server_ip,
  quantile(0.5)(latency_ms) AS median_ms
FROM smokeping.v_dig
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts)
  AND dns_server_ip != ''
  AND agent_location IN (${location:sqlstring})
  AND target_name    IN (${target:sqlstring})
GROUP BY time, dns_server_ip
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Answered A/AAAA records
panels.description: Every address returned for each name, with when it was last seen. A record quietly repointed to a different CDN shows up here as a new row.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  target_name        AS "Name",
  answer_ip          AS "Answer IP",
  any(dns_status)    AS "Status",
  any(authoritative) AS "Authoritative",
  count()            AS "Observations",
  min(ts)            AS "First seen",
  max(ts)            AS "Last seen"
FROM smokeping.v_dig
ARRAY JOIN answer_ips AS answer_ip
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts)
  AND agent_location IN (${location:sqlstring})
  AND target_name    IN (${target:sqlstring})
GROUP BY target_name, answer_ip
ORDER BY "Name", "Observations" DESC
LIMIT 200

panels.title: Failed measurements
panels.description: Failures are stored, not discarded — with the timeout or error message that caused them.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  ts                 AS "Time",
  agent_location     AS "From",
  probe              AS "Probe",
  target_group       AS "Group",
  target_name        AS "Target",
  target             AS "Address",
  resolved_ip        AS "Resolved IP",
  error_type         AS "Error",
  error_message      AS "Detail"
FROM smokeping.measurements
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts)
  AND success = 0
  AND agent_location IN (${location:sqlstring})
  AND probe          IN (${probe:sqlstring})
  AND target_name    IN (${target:sqlstring})
ORDER BY ts DESC
LIMIT 200
